## Summary

- **`postJson` return type simplified**: was returning `{ response, payload }` but every caller only used `payload`. Now returns `Promise<unknown>` directly; all 10 call sites updated across 6 files.
- **HTTP error handling added**: `postJson` now throws with the actual HTTP status (`HTTP 500 Internal Server Error`) on non-OK responses instead of silently proceeding to JSON parsing and emitting a misleading error.
- **JSON parse error improved**: when a 2xx response has a non-JSON body the error now includes the HTTP status for easier debugging.
- **`DEFAULT_IMAGE_SIZE` consolidated**: moved from a local constant in `image-generation-pipeline.ts` into `SYSTEM_CONSTANTS` in `constants.ts` where all cross-seam config already lives.

## Test plan

- [ ] `npm run check` — 0 errors, 0 warnings
- [ ] `npm run test` — 417 tests pass, 1 skipped (integration, env-gated)
- [ ] `http-client.test.ts` updated: added non-OK HTTP status test, updated return-value assertions for new signature

## Summary by Sourcery

Simplify the JSON HTTP client helper, improve its error reporting, and consolidate an image size constant into shared system configuration.

Bug Fixes:
- Ensure non-OK HTTP responses from postJson throw errors that include the HTTP status and status text.
- Include HTTP status information in errors when JSON parsing of successful responses fails.

Enhancements:
- Change postJson to return the parsed JSON payload directly instead of a response/payload wrapper object.
- Update all call sites to consume the simplified postJson return value.
- Use a shared DEFAULT_IMAGE_SIZE value from SYSTEM_CONSTANTS in the image generation pipeline instead of a local constant.

Tests:
- Extend http-client tests to cover non-OK HTTP status handling and the updated error messaging, and adjust assertions for the new postJson return type.

Hey - I've found 2 issues, and left some high level feedback:

- Consider making `postJson` generic (e.g. `postJson<T>(...): Promise<T>`) so callers can get strongly-typed responses instead of `unknown` and avoid repeated casting or schema parsing boilerplate.
- The new HTTP error messages in `postJson` could be more actionable if they included the request URL and optionally a short snippet of the response body when available, to make debugging server issues easier.

## Overall Comments
- Consider making `postJson` generic (e.g. `postJson<T>(...): Promise<T>`) so callers can get strongly-typed responses instead of `unknown` and avoid repeated casting or schema parsing boilerplate.
- The new HTTP error messages in `postJson` could be more actionable if they included the request URL and optionally a short snippet of the response body when available, to make debugging server issues easier.

</code_context>
<issue_to_address>
**suggestion:** Consider making `postJson` generic so callers can get a typed payload instead of `unknown`.

Returning `Promise<unknown>` forces every caller to cast or refine, which weakens type safety. You can instead make this function generic, e.g. `export const postJson = async <T>(url: string, body: unknown): Promise<T> => { ... }`, and let callers specify `postJson<MeechieToolResult>(...)` etc. This preserves runtime behavior while improving compile-time guarantees and avoiding repeated `unknown` casts.
</issue_to_address>

### Comment 2
<location path="src/lib/core/http-client.ts" line_range="18-19" />
<code_context>
+	if (!response.ok) {
+		throw new Error(`postJson: HTTP ${response.status} ${response.statusText}`);
+	}
+	return response.json().catch(() => {
+		throw new Error(`postJson: HTTP ${response.status} - failed to parse response as JSON`);
 	});
-	return { response, payload };
</code_context>
<issue_to_address>
**issue:** JSON parsing will throw for valid `204 No Content` or empty-body responses, which might be an unintended edge case.

For successful responses with no body (e.g. 204, possibly 205, or 200 with an empty body), `response.json()` will reject and surface a parse error even though the request succeeded. Consider explicitly handling `response.status === 204` (and similar cases) or checking for an empty body and returning `undefined` instead of attempting JSON parsing.
</issue_to_address>
~~~
